title: 因果推断
scope: Intervention effects, observational identification, confounding, temporal ordering and quasi-experimental assumptions.
routingDescription: Intervention effects, observational identification, confounding, temporal ordering and quasi-experimental assumptions.
useWhen: Explain whether an intervention caused a change
Compare rollout groups with non-random timing

distinguishFrom.criterion: Use statistical inference for estimation without an intervention claim.
Use experiment design for a future controlled trial.

diagnosticChecklist.check: Specify intervention, outcome, population, counterfactual comparison and time horizon.
diagnosticChecklist.decisionImpact: Keep the causal estimand separate from an observed association.

diagnosticChecklist.check: State the causal ordering and identification assumptions; check confounders, mediators and colliders.
diagnosticChecklist.decisionImpact: Do not turn regression adjustment into proof of causality.

diagnosticChecklist.check: Check selection, comparability and treatment overlap before choosing an estimator.
diagnosticChecklist.decisionImpact: Limit the target population or acknowledge non-identification when support is absent.

diagnosticChecklist.when: When adoption is staggered or outcomes trend over time
diagnosticChecklist.check: Check treatment timing, pre-trends, anticipation, concurrent changes and heterogeneous effects.
diagnosticChecklist.decisionImpact: Qualify difference-in-differences or fixed-effects recommendations with their assumptions.

diagnosticChecklist.when: When key assumptions cannot be observed
diagnosticChecklist.check: Name a discriminating test, negative control, sensitivity analysis or design change.
diagnosticChecklist.decisionImpact: Report bounded conclusions and what evidence would change them.

evidenceRequirements: Selection mechanism and relevant potential confounders
qualityChecks: No causal uplift from a before/after difference alone
A passing pre-trend test does not prove parallel trends or eliminate unmeasured confounding
riskRules: Policy, health and financial intervention recommendations require domain review of consequential assumptions

preferredSources: Original identification and estimation references for the selected causal design
Domain evidence for treatment assignment, temporal ordering and plausible confounding
refreshTriggers: Design-specific methodological guidance and applicable domain rules
knowledgePolicy.onMissing: Bound the conclusion and state which current source or evidence is needed.

examples.input: Sites adopt a feature in different weeks while also running region-specific promotions.
examples.expected: Examine timing, confounding, comparability and pre-trends before attributing uplift.
examples.reject: Claim causal impact from pooled treated-versus-control means.
